clue.text: Female coming in drunk, about to start this quarrel

explanation.surface: A woman stumbles in tipsy, and a row is about to break out.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym, informal: a vicious spat, especially one between two women, is likened to fighting cats.

clue.text: Competent personal assistant introduced to lead

clue.text: A large amount of acid salt

parts.note: tart means sharp or acid in taste

explanation.surface: Lots of acid salt, as in a chemistry lab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' is an old sailor, not sodium chloride.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword-friendly sense: an old salt and a jack tar are both names for a sailor.

clue.text: Most of old auditors worked, being devoted to figures

indicators.note: the letters are worked over into a fresh order
the final letter of the word is dropped

explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' takes OL from OLD; 'worked' rearranges OLAUDITORS.
explanation.definitionFit: A cunning sense: worshipping idols, statues or images, so devoted to figures in the sense of carved effigies.

clue.text: Stash of treasure, much of it years old

clue.text: Christian's taken craft prize

a reward or premium paid out, as for capturing a fugitive

explanation.surface: A believer has stolen a boat as a trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: Fletcher Christian led the mutiny on the Bounty, so 'Christian' is a man's surname, not a believer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the mutineers' ship, and a reward money offered for something achieved.

clue.text: Polish round mounted gemstone

explanation.surface: A jeweller polishes a round stone set in a mounting.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a milky iridescent stone used in jewellery.

clue.text: Unusual type of balsam seen around on group of trees

clue.text: My radar is faulty in position above the deck

indicators.note: a broken device gives scrambled output, so the letters are rearranged

clue.text: Greatest power lies in shrewd industrial action

P for power, as in physics

clue.text: Fitness coach working on a real sprinter

explanation.surface: A gym coach is busy training a genuine runner.

clue.text: What prevents extraction by an oil-producing plant? That's coming across unknown primate

clue.text: Regularly observed Neptunian feature spewing lava

clue.text: Reliable person has a job with small baking outfit

work means job
S for small, as a clothing size

clue.text: Cutting less is just about the end of Labour

explanation.walkthrough: 'just about' puts R, the last letter of Labour, inside EXCEPT.

clue.text: A mystery, perhaps, where small stream feeds into the river

parts.note: a rill is a brook

explanation.surface: A local objector's pal blocks the building of a new motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: NIMBY stands for 'not in my back yard', a protester against local development; the clue's 'Perhaps' makes it an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the letters of not-in-my-back-yard are pronounced as a word, so it is a word built from initials.

clue.text: Revolutionary challenge removing the last man on board

clue.text: Make fast English tea around noon at home

clue.text: Drama about wickets before being out of the running
